monza.name: Autodromo Nazionale di Monza
history: Built in 1922 inside Monza Park, it is one of the oldest permanent circuits in the world and has hosted the Italian Grand Prix since the very dawn of motorsport.

The current layout alternates lightning-fast straights with technical chicanes, with the Parabolica as the final, iconic corner before the finish line. The low drag required makes it one of the highest average-speed tracks on the calendar.

spa-francorchamps.name: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
spa-francorchamps.tagline: Amid the hills of the Ardennes
history: Opened in 1921 on public roads between the villages of Francorchamps, Stavelot and Malmedy, it is one of the longest and most respected circuits in world motorsport, set deep in the Ardennes forest.
It's famous for Eau Rouge-Raidillon, the uphill sequence of corners linking the valley floor to the rest of the track, and for weather that often changes dramatically from one sector to the next.

silverstone.name: Silverstone Circuit
history: Built on a former RAF airfield, Silverstone hosted the first Grand Prix of the newly founded Formula 1 World Championship in 1950.
The track is famous for the high-speed sequence of Maggotts, Becketts and Chapel, one of the most demanding corner combinations on the calendar for balance and aerodynamics.

nurburgring-nordschleife.name: Nürburgring Nordschleife
history: Opened in 1927 amid the hills of the Eifel, the old Nordschleife track winds for about 20 km through elevation changes, blind corners and constantly shifting grip, earning it the nickname 'Grüne Hölle' (Green Hell), coined by Jackie Stewart.

After Niki Lauda's severe crash in 1976, Formula 1 abandoned the long track in favour of the shorter GP-Strecke, but the Nordschleife remains a legendary proving ground for the automotive industry and for endurance races like the 24 Hours of Nürburgring.

le-mans.name: Circuit de la Sarthe
le-mans.tagline: Home of the 24 Hours of Le Mans
history: The Circuit de la Sarthe combines a permanent track with long stretches of public roads closed to traffic, and has been the stage for the 24 Hours of Le Mans since 1923, the most prestigious endurance race in the world.
It's famous for the Ligne Droite des Hunaudières (the Mulsanne Straight), once taken flat out before two chicanes were introduced in the 1990s for safety reasons.

suzuka.name: Suzuka Circuit
history: Designed by Dutch engineer John Hugenholtz and opened in 1962 as a Honda test track, Suzuka is famous for its figure-eight layout, with an overpass that makes the track cross over itself.
Corners like 130R and Spoon Curve demand pinpoint precision, and for years the circuit hosted the Japanese Grand Prix at a pivotal point of the Formula 1 season.
